t: Notwithstanding the amendments made by this title, part 2 of subchapter C of chapter VII of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, as in effect on the day before the date of the enactment of this title, shall continue to be in effect with respect to human drug applications and supplements (as defined in such part as of such day) that on or after October 1, 2012, but before October 1, 2017, were accepted by the Food and Drug Administration for filing with respect to assessing and collecting any fee required by such part for a fiscal year prior to fiscal year 2018.

fable.w: This is a savings clause that keeps the prior user-fee provisions in effect for human drug applications accepted for filing during a set period, so that fees can still be assessed and collected. The tempting reading is that drug applications filed by companies with the FDA involve outside parties, but applications are expressly excluded from participation. Nothing here requires consultation, comment, a hearing, an advisory body, rulemaking, or a right to sue.
fable.s: shall continue to be in effect with respect to human drug applications and supplements

opus.w: This is a savings clause that keeps the earlier user-fee rules in effect for drug applications filed in a set period. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The mention of drug applications filed by companies is a trap: applying for approval is not participating in a federal decision.
opus.s: shall continue to be in effect with respect to human drug applications and supplements (as defined in such part as of such day) that on or after October 1, 2012, but before October 1, 2017, were accepted by the Food and Drug Administration for filing with respect to assessing and collecting any fee
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that "human drug applications and supplements" submitted to and "accepted by the Food and Drug Administration" are a way for outside companies to take part in a federal decision. That fails against the definition: an application for a license or approval is not participation. Also, this provision is only a transition (savings) clause. It keeps the old fee rules in place for applications accepted between October 1, 2012 and October 1, 2017. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue appears.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section addresses the applicability of fee collection rules for human drug applications already accepted by the FDA. The definition explicitly excludes 'applications for benefits or grants' (and regulatory applications) from the scope of participation. There is no requirement for consultation, public comment, or advisory input from outside parties in this text; it is purely a procedural provision regarding fees and filing dates.
qwen_chat.s: part 2 of subchapter C of chapter VII of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act... shall continue to be in effect with respect to human drug applications and supplements... that on or after October 1, 2012, but before October 1, 2017, were accepted by the Food and Drug Administration for filing with respect to assessing and collecting any fee
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section mentions "human drug applications" submitted by companies (outside parties), it involves participation. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits or grants" (and by extension, regulatory applications like drug approvals) are not participation. The section merely defines the temporal scope of fee collection rules for existing applications; it does not create a new process for outside parties to consult, comment, or advise on a federal decision.
